title: Genre Study - Film as Literature
description: Introduces students to films and literature in general, screenwriting, how the written word is translated to the screen, how the written word in another language is translated, and cultural and historical aspects of adaptation.

title: Genre Study - Short Stories
description: Humans are a story telling animal. We seem to need them to make sense of ourselves. In this course we will read short stories from some of the world famous masters and innovators of the form (e.g. Chekhov, D.H. Lawrence, Gogol, Heinrich von Kleist, Mishima, Verga) to a sampling of contemporary writers (Lucia Berlin, Dagoberto Gilb, Junot Diaz, Aimee Bender, Gunnhild Oyehaug). The readings vary in tone, style, theme, language, and degrees of realism, surrealism, magic realism, and absurdism. Students will write carefully crafted responses to stories as well as short stories of their own.

title: Advanced Literary Criticism in Theory and Practice
description: This course provides students with an advanced understanding of the theory and practice of literary criticism. Course readings represent a wide range of methodologies and models for interpretation, including New Criticism, New Historicism, Feminism, Queer theory, and Postcolonialism, among others. Students will pursue advanced projects in literary criticism informed by their knowledge of the theoretical basis for their explorations and the practices of other literary and cultural critics. Although there are no specific prerequisites for the course, students will be expected to read and respond to challenging texts in both oral and written discussion, including reading responses and a large-scale (ten pages or more) work of scholarship.

title: Reading Like a Writer - Thematic Study
description: Invites students to complete intensive reading on a single theme from the perspective of a writer. Students focus on how the elements of the theme might apply to their own work.

title: Reading Like a Writer - Thematic Study - Afrofuturism Past, Present, and Future
description: Introduces students to Afrofuturism, a speculative fiction genre that uses features from fantasy, science fiction, horror, and folk tales to craft narratives that center the experiences of Africans and members of the African diaspora.

title: Reading Like a Writer - Thematic Study: Portrait of an Artist as a Young Person
description: Invites students to complete intensive reading on a single theme from the perspective of a writer. Students focus on how the elements of the theme might apply to their own work.

title: Reading Like a Writer - Thematic Study: Spiritual Poetry: Rumi, Rilke, and Dickenson
description: Invites students to complete intensive reading on a single theme from the perspective of a writer. Students focus on how the elements of the theme might apply to their own work.

title: Reading Like a Writer - Thematic Study - UCSB Reads
description: Invites students to complete intensive reading on a single theme from the perspective of a writer. Students focus on how the elements of the theme might apply to their own work. This iteration focuses on the UCSB Reads selection.

title: Topics in Writing Studies
description: Intensive study of varying topics in the field of writing studies.

title: Topics in Writing Studies
description: Intensive study of varying topics in the field of writing studies.

title: Topics in Writing Studies - Creative Writing Studies
description: Study of the practice and theories of creative writing.

title: Topics in Writing Studies - Development of the Writer
description: Writers develop their thinking, feeling, and perception through their writing throughout their life. To begin to unpack the complex puzzle of how this happens and what its implications are, we need tools of careful reading, psychology, sociology, cultural studies, and history.

title: Topics in Writing Studies - Facts, Fake Facts, and Non-Facts: Method in the inscription
description: Intensive study of varying topics in the field of writing studies. This instance focuses on Facts, Fake Facts, and Non-Facts: Method in the inscription.

title: Linguistic Justice
description: W&L CS 160LJ, Linguistic Justice, focuses on how Writing Studies as a discipline approaches issues of language with a focus on justice. Rhetoric is such a key part of Writing Studies, so we will look at rhetorical situations that deal specifically with linguistic choices and expectations. Because this class will be taught at UCSB, which has both HSI and AAPI designations, we will investigate the linguistic injustices facing these communities and others in US classrooms, communities, and the larger political sphere. Issues of accessibility will also be addressed. Students can expect to read a mixture of public and academic scholarship on these topics and to engage in written genres that address both audiences.

title: Topics in Writing Studies - Dominant Discourses in Literacy Narratives
description: This course invites students to critically investigate literacy narratives, drawing upon research methods in writing studies such as archival work, rhetorical and content analysis. Students collect and analyze data, and work towards a publishable research article.

title: Rhetoric of Reproductive Justice
description: This course is structured around the three major tenets of reproductive justice—the right to have children, the right to not have children, and the right to parent children in safe and healthy environments. Students will engage with each of these tenets through readings and assignments that focus on the rhetorical, cultural, and historical significance of these three core elements to the ever expanding field of reproductive justice.

title: Topics in Writing Studies - STEM Stories
description: Drawing upon research in writing studies, this course examines the work that stories (narratives) do within various STEM contexts. All majors, and all levels of STEM expertise, are welcome.

title: Topics in Multimedia Writing
description: Intensive study of varying topics in the area of multimedia writing in the field of writing studies.

title: Topics in Multimedia Writing: Digital Storytelling
description: Intensive study of varying topics in the area of multimedia writing in the field of writing studies.

title: Topics in Multimedia Writing: New Media
description: Intensive study of varying topics in the area of multimedia writing in the field of writing studies. Blogs, Podcasts, and Video Essays.

title: Literary Publishing
description: Full-year course offering instruction in literary publication. Students apply what they learn to creating the CCS literary magazines Spectrum and Into the Teeth of the Wind or to an independent project. Topics covered include establishing an editorial perspective, developing and soliciting content, promotion, document design and layout, and strategies for copyediting.

title: Introduction of Literary Publishing
description: Students are introduced to the art and business of literary publishing in preparation for work on Spectrum Literary Journal and careers in writing or publishing.

title: Literary Publishing: Selection
description: Students read and select works to be published from submissions to Spectrum Literary Journal. Topics covered include establishing an editorial perspective, developing and soliciting content.

title: Literary Publishing: Copyediting and Design
description: Students copyedit works to be published in Spectrum Literary Journal and design the annual issue. Topics covered include promotion, document design and layout, and strategies for copyediting.

title: The Writer's Life
description: Students are exposed to potential professional applications of the Writing and Literature major through appropriate guest lectures, readings, and experiential learning opportunities.

title: Junior Tutorial
description: Students work independently with their faculty advisor to develop information and expertise necessary for their senior portfolio. May include training in methods, apprenticeship experience, or independent reading and coursework.

title: Writer's Studio
description: Dedicated workspace for students to pursue independent projects in consultation with faculty and peer consultants

title: Teaching Practicum
description: Advanced instruction in the pedagogy of writing while assisting in W&L 191 under faculty supervision.

title: Senior Portfolio
description: Students work independently with their faculty advisor to complete their senior portfolio.

title: Internship
description: Academic credit for professional experience with an approved organization or individual.
